MODULE 5 - Issue Status Tracking - Five-state lifecycle (OPEN → IN_PROGRESS →
PENDING_ACTION → RESOLVED → CLOSED) enforced server-side with a
legal-transition map; closed issues can never be reopened (a new issue must be
created instead).

MODULE 5 - Role-Based Access Control - Partners see only their own issues; QE full-access
roles (IT/Admin/CS/SM/CSM/Leadership) see all issues; QE SR/RSM are
territory-scoped, matching how orders and invoices are already scoped
elsewhere in the portal.

MODULE 5 - Internal Task Board - QE-only kanban board
(OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/BLOCKED/COMPLETED columns) for assigning and
tracking investigation tasks per issue, with status-colored cards and a required
reason when marking a task Blocked.

MODULE 5 -  Comment Thread with Internal/Partner Visibility - Shared comment thread where
QE staff can post internal-only notes (hidden from partners, enforced server-side,
not just in the UI) or partner-visible updates; messages are chat-style aligned and
color-coded by who posted them (Partner vs. QE Team).

MODULE 5 -  Activity Timeline - Chronological log of all status changes and comments per
issue, shown in a sticky sidebar on the detail page.

MODULE 5 -  Real-Time Comment/Timeline Updates - Comments and timeline refresh
automatically every few seconds without a manual page reload, so QE and
partner conversations stay in sync.

MODULE 5 -  Resolution Authorization Workflow - QE staff can authorize a resolution
(Replacement, Refund, Repair, Partial Credit, or Write-Off) on an issue;
resolutions under $500 can be authorized by any issue-triage role, while $500 or
more requires QE SM or QE IT approval specifically.

MODULE 5 -  Manual JDE Reference Tracking - Resolution form captures a manually-entered
SO number, credit memo number, or tracking number (whatever QE staff already
created directly in JDE) — no automated write-back to JDE in this version.

MODULE 5 -  Partner Resolution Confirmation - Once a resolution is authorized, the partner
sees a "Confirm Resolution" button; confirming closes the issue out and logs it in
the timeline.

MODULE 5 -  Email Notifications - Automatic emails on issue creation, status changes,
action-needed requests, and resolution-ready events.

MODULE 5 - Issue Metrics Dashboard - QE-only analytics page (/issues/dashboard) showing
total issues, breakdowns by status/type/severity, average resolution time, and top
accounts by issue volume.

MODULE 5 - Sidebar Navigation Entry - Added an "Issues" link inside the Account dropdown
menu, gated by a new "View Issues" permission so only roles explicitly granted
that permission can see or access it.

axios client, not the destination API. The string is generated locally when no
response arrives within the configured window; src/config/index.ts sets a 30s
timeout that feeds both JDE clients. Confirmed against logs/error.log that the
underlying slowness is on the JDE side, not in how we send requests.

run slower than ordering, and both recent orchestration timeouts (2026-07-21)

client's timeout changed; orders remains at 30s. Configurable via the new
DESTINATION_QUOTE_API_TIMEOUT.

module_detail.name: CFC - Studio inline editing not working

notes: Setup the CFC repo locally to verify if issue also persists in local environment but it wasn't reproducible (working). After rechecking the workflow again, found that the issue was caused by domain mismatch: https://new-website.communityfoodclubgr.org/ VS https://stackshift-cfccommunityfoodclub-je80.webriq.me/. The studio auto login workflow from the StackShift app via Launch Experience gets the originating URL of the studio and sets an auto login token for the current session. Right now we're having different URLs - the inline editor URL doesn't match the originating URL where the token was added, hence why the editor fields have become read-only showing "Your roles do not have permissions to update this document". Checked the environment variables NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_STUDIO_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and updated with the LIVE URL then redeployed. The inline editor works now. Added the completed details to task comment and informed Niña about this as well.

After installing, run yarn build to confirm current code base builds as expected; 5.
If all good, finally run command yarn generate]. Confirmed issue was resolved after going through these steps.

notes: Worked on issue reported on published changes not reflected for the WebriQ website. Found that it was caused by the Vercel deploy not automatically triggered to bump up new changes. module_detail.name: StackShift project | SwampFox - Netlify build error

notes: Helped investigate and resolve the Netlify build errors for the SwampFox deploy. Based on the Netlify documentation following the build log as clue https://docs.netlify.com/environment-variables/secrets-controller/#configure-secrets-scanning, added a new ENV variable SECRETS_SCAN_OMIT_PATHS and added the .netlify build cache folder path and redeployed project without cache. Confirmed after steps done the build issue was now resolved: https://app.netlify.com/projects/dxp-site-swampfoxoptics-u93r/deploys

module_detail.name: StackShift Updates - Upgrade to latest Next.js version

notes:
From a dev branch on StackShift default, started to upgrade the Next.js version to latest and React version to 18.3.1 (instead of v19)
https://github.com/webriq-pagebuilder/site-template-default/pull/298/commits/5b4314276cfe183d63003bb6d05f6ece8c567550 and tested from local environment if all is still working from StackShift studio to preview. I got runtime preview errors when opening /studio and home page after the update. Tried to run the codemod thinking it was caused by the warnings on the async-api changes https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-async-request-api but still the issue persists. Eventually lead to a fix by removing the "--turbopack" option when running the "yarn dev" command and revised the schema file by moving the top-level asynchronous call to resolve the runtime errors https://github.com/webriq-pagebuilder/site-template-default/pull/298/commits/6dbe0556a08cbb95080334e4be7b17505b0e8d84. I kept the next-sanity version to the current since we don't intend to upgrade the Sanity version to latest and have verified with the current dev branch setup that all are working from the studio to site preview as usual.
